title: Patient Complaints, Boundaries, and Urgent Escalation

sections.learningObjectives:
- Handle patient complaints professionally using active listening, empathy, accurate documentation, and office policy.
- Maintain professional boundaries in person, on the phone, and through electronic and social media, protecting patient confidentiality.
- Distinguish service complaints from urgent clinical concerns by recognizing red-flag symptoms and statements.
- Escalate urgent clinical concerns immediately to licensed staff and follow the office chain of command.
- Stay within the medical office assistant scope of practice by relaying information without diagnosing, triaging, or giving medical advice.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

When a friend is upset, the kindest thing to do first is to really listen and say you understand before trying to fix anything.

### Question 2

If someone is shouting, you stay calm and say, 'Let's step somewhere quiet to talk about it' instead of shouting back or pretending they are not there.

### Question 3

Active listening is like giving someone your whole attention when they talk, then repeating back what they said so they know you really got it.

### Question 4

If a customer says a store charged them twice, the cashier writes it down and sends it to the right person instead of promising the money back themselves.

### Question 5

Even when someone is mean, a professional stays calm and says, 'I want to help, but please speak to me respectfully,' then keeps trying to fix the problem.

### Question 6

Writing a problem down is like making a note so the right person can fix it later, and so everyone knows what really happened.

### Question 7

You can say 'I'm sorry that felt bad' without saying 'I did something wrong' - you are caring about how they feel, not confessing.

### Question 8

If a classmate says a teacher was unfair, a good friend listens and helps them talk to the right grown-up instead of calling the teacher names.

### Question 9

If someone slips on the sidewalk at school, the right thing is to tell a teacher right away and write down what happened - you don't just offer them a sticker.

### Question 10

A complaint box is for fixing problems and making the place better, not for getting people in trouble or hiding problems.

### Question 11

When someone is upset, your body should say 'I'm listening and I care' - stand open, look at them, and stay calm.

### Question 12

When two people remember a game differently, you don't fight about it - you each say what you remember and let a referee sort it out.

### Question 13

If the same playground slide keeps causing scrapes, you tell the principal so they can fix the slide instead of ignoring it.

### Question 14

If a customer asks for the manager, a good worker calmly says, 'Sure, let me get them for you' instead of making excuses.

### Question 15

Saying 'I'm sorry that felt bad' is about caring how someone feels, not about saying you broke something.

### Question 16

If a student has a problem with a teacher, you tell the principal and let them handle it - you don't give out the teacher's home number or spread gossip.

### Question 17

Sometimes a kid is upset about a broken toy but is really scared about something else - a good helper fixes what they can and calls an adult for the scary part.

### Question 18

If a friend is upset, letting them finish their sentence helps you understand what is really wrong instead of guessing.

### Question 19

A sealed note is private - you hand it to the right grown-up, you don't read it out loud or toss it in the trash.

### Question 20

If someone's private diary went missing at school, you would tell the teacher right away because private information was not protected.

### Question 21

A service complaint is like 'the line was too long,' while a clinical concern is like 'I feel sick' - only the second one needs a doctor right away.

### Question 22

If a friend asks whether they need a certain repair, you don't decide for them - you help them talk to the mechanic about the cost.

### Question 23

Everyone on a team helps when a customer has a problem - each person does their part and passes it to the right person when needed.

### Question 24

When a friend is talking to you, you finish listening to them before grabbing another conversation.

### Question 25

If someone says the rules were broken, you tell the referee or teacher so the official process can decide - you don't just ignore it or decide yourself.

### Question 26

Boundaries are like the fence around a schoolyard - they keep everyone safe while still letting people play and talk together.

### Question 27

A teacher wouldn't give a student their private phone number - they'd say, 'You can reach me through the school.'

### Question 28

Just like a teacher keeps their online life separate from students, a medical assistant keeps patients out of their personal online world.

### Question 29

If someone gives you a big gift at work, you check the rules first - most jobs say no thanks for big gifts, but you say it kindly.

### Question 30

If a student keeps following one teacher everywhere and telling them secrets, the teacher politely keeps it about school and tells the principal.

### Question 31

A coach wouldn't date a player - they'd kindly say no and keep things about the team, telling the boss if it keeps happening.

### Question 32

A good helper talks about the person they are helping, not all about their own life.

### Question 33

If a friend tells you something that could hurt them, the caring thing is to tell a trusted grown-up, not to promise to hide it.

### Question 34

If a friend says something that makes you worry they are not safe, the right thing is to get a trusted adult to help right away.

### Question 35

If you find yourself thinking about work too much, you talk to a trusted adult to get back to a healthy balance.

### Question 36

Scope of practice is like the list of jobs you are trained and allowed to do - you do those jobs and call the expert for the rest.

### Question 37

You wouldn't guess what a strange spot is - you'd show it to the doctor who is trained to figure it out.

### Question 38

Only the person with the right training can approve medicine - you pass the request to the doctor or nurse.

### Question 39

You wouldn't share a friend's private information with just anyone who asks - you first make sure they are allowed to know.

### Question 40

You can be kind to a customer without becoming their personal assistant outside of work.

### Question 41

A fence protects everyone in the yard, not just one person.

### Question 42

When a game gets tiring, a good player takes a break, asks the coach for help, and keeps playing fair instead of getting mad at everyone.

### Question 43

Stepping a little over the line by accident is different from running far past it on purpose and hurting someone.

### Question 44

If a friend keeps giving you treats every day, you might kindly say, 'That's so sweet, but you really don't have to.'

### Question 45

You only tell a secret to the people who truly need to know to help, not to everyone who asks.

### Question 46

You wouldn't talk about a friend's secret where other kids could hear, even if your friend isn't there.

### Question 47

If someone keeps asking you out after you said no, you stay firm and tell a trusted adult for help.

### Question 48

You wouldn't give a stranger a ride home from work - you'd help them call a cab or a family member.

### Question 49

The rules of being a good friend apply whether you are together, on the phone, or texting.

### Question 50

A teacher wouldn't be in a student's will or be their emergency contact - that's too personal for a work relationship.

### Question 51

An urgent concern is when someone's body might need a doctor's help soon, not when they are just grumpy about the wait.

### Question 52

If someone on the phone says their chest hurts, you stop everything and get a nurse or doctor right away - it's that serious.

### Question 53

If a friend says their head hurts worse than ever before, out of nowhere, you don't tell them to nap - you get help fast.

### Question 54

If someone has trouble breathing, you don't wait around - you get a grown-up with medical training right now.

### Question 55

You wouldn't decide a fire alarm is 'probably nothing' - you'd let the firefighter check it out.

### Question 56

If a friend says they might faint, you sit them down so they don't fall, then run for help.

### Question 57

If a friend says, 'Oh, and I'm bleeding a lot,' you stop talking about plans and get help for the bleeding first.

### Question 58

If someone on the phone can't breathe, you never put them on hold - you get help for them right that second.

### Question 59

Chest pain, trouble breathing, and a droopy face are the body's alarm bells - they always mean 'get a doctor now.'

### Question 60

A droopy face and numb side are like a fire alarm - you act fast and call for help, you don't tell them to rest.

### Question 61

If a friend waiting in line says they feel worse and worse, you don't just say 'hang on' - you check what's wrong and get help.

### Question 62

If a medicine makes someone feel weird, you tell the doctor or nurse right away - you never tell them to stop or take more on your own.

### Question 63

You tell the teacher what you saw right away and let them decide what it means - you don't keep it to yourself.

### Question 64

If a friend talks about hurting themselves, you stay with them and get a trusted adult to help right away - you never ignore it.

### Question 65

If a friend says their problem is getting worse and no one is listening, the first thing is to make sure someone finally helps with the problem.

### Question 66

If someone's face swells after a new medicine, that's an emergency - you get help fast, you don't wait and see.

### Question 67

Escalating is like pulling the fire alarm - you tell the people who can help right away, not next week.

### Question 68

If someone says their chest feels heavy, you drop what you're doing and get help - nothing on your screen is more important.

### Question 69

If a friend says they just feel 'off' and look worried, you don't brush it off - you keep an eye on them and get help if needed.

### Question 70

If a friend fell and now feels dizzy, you get them checked out - a bump on the head can hide a real problem.

### Question 71

When there's an emergency, you tell the doctor or nurse - the people trained to help - not just anyone nearby.

### Question 72

When you tell a grown-up something is wrong, you say who, what's happening, and where they are - so help arrives fast.

### Question 73

If the kitchen is on fire, you don't finish washing dishes first - you put out the fire now.

### Question 74

If a kid insists they need the doctor right now, you tell the nurse and let the nurse decide - you don't decide they're fine or promise them a spot.

### Question 75

If the main teacher is busy, you tell the helper teacher - you don't just wait or try to fix it yourself.

### Question 76

After you tell a grown-up something important, you write down what you said, who you told, and when - so nothing gets lost.

### Question 77

When someone can't breathe, you get the medical team right away - you don't ask them to fill out forms.

### Question 78

If you're not sure whether something is a big deal, you ask a grown-up - better safe than sorry.

### Question 79

You can whisper a private problem to the teacher instead of shouting it across the room - still fast, but private.

### Question 80

Escalating is saying 'there's a problem - please look,' while diagnosing is the doctor deciding what the problem is.

### Question 81

If a friend suddenly starts acting confused, you tell a grown-up right away - it could mean something is wrong.

### Question 82

If you're not sure a smoke smell is a fire, you don't decide it's nothing - you tell someone who can check.

### Question 83

After you tell the teacher about a problem, you stay nearby to help and write down what happened - you don't just walk away.

### Question 84

In an emergency, you follow the drill - call for help and get the medical team, just like a fire drill.

### Question 85

When several things happen at once, a good helper stays calm, doesn't make promises they can't keep, and gets help for the scary part first.
